scene_1_pastrana_park_morning_walk.speaker: Rose
scene_1_pastrana_park_morning_walk.text: \Raya do Pastrana Park. \Tanan nag \tawo ga \tikang iya kon \agahon.
scene_1_pastrana_park_morning_walk.translation: This is Pastrana Park. Everyone walks here in the morning.

scene_1_pastrana_park_morning_walk.speaker: Player
scene_1_pastrana_park_morning_walk.text: It's nice here. Peaceful, unlike the busy streets in the States.

scene_1_pastrana_park_morning_walk.speaker: Rose
scene_1_pastrana_park_morning_walk.text: Wait until festival season. Not peaceful at all then. But that's later.
An old man selling dried fish smiles and waves at Rose.

scene_1_pastrana_park_morning_walk.speaker: Rose
scene_1_pastrana_park_morning_walk.text: Ruyon, si Anong Pedring. \Suki namon \igto sa tindahan.
scene_1_pastrana_park_morning_walk.translation: That's Anong Pedring. He's our regular vendor at the market.

scene_1_pastrana_park_morning_walk.text: Will you talk to Anong Pedring?

choices.label: Good morning! I'm here with Jonabel's family.
Uh, hi. Sorry, I'm still nervous speaking Akeanon.
I'll just wait here, you go ahead.

scene_1_pastrana_park_morning_walk.speaker: Anong Pedring
scene_1_pastrana_park_morning_walk.text: \Mayad-ayad nga agahon! \Apo gali ni Jonabel. \Siin ka \halin?

scene_1_pastrana_park_morning_walk.speaker: Rose
scene_1_pastrana_park_morning_walk.text: Suit yourself. But you'll have to talk to people eventually.

scene_1_pastrana_park_morning_walk.speaker: Rose
scene_1_pastrana_park_morning_walk.text: \Sunod \kamo sa market. Iya kita \magtuon it mga \pangaean.
scene_1_pastrana_park_morning_walk.translation: Follow us to the market. This is where we'll learn some names of things.

scene_2_kalibo_public_market.text: The market is full of color and noise — fruits, fish, cloth, everything mixed together. The smell of dried fish and freshly cooked rice fills the air.

scene_2_kalibo_public_market.speaker: Anong Pedring
scene_2_kalibo_public_market.translation: What do you want, grandchild? There's plenty here — rice, water, fish.

scene_2_kalibo_public_market.speaker: Player
scene_2_kalibo_public_market.text: Rose, how do I say I want this?

scene_2_kalibo_public_market.speaker: Rose
scene_2_kalibo_public_market.text: Say "\pangabay" first. Means please. Basic manners, balikbayan.
Player points at a round fruit, unfamiliar.

scene_2_kalibo_public_market.speaker: Anong Pedring
scene_2_kalibo_public_market.translation: Star-shaped fruit — star fruit, grandchild. Very sweet.

choices.label: Yes, pangabay, I'd like to try it.
Maybe later, let me look around first.
I'm okay, I'm not a fan of exotic fruits, sorry.

scene_2_kalibo_public_market.speaker: Anong Pedring
scene_2_kalibo_public_market.text: That's fine, my goods won't disappear quickly.

scene_2_kalibo_public_market.speaker: Rose
scene_2_kalibo_public_market.text: Your loss. This is literally one of the best things here.

scene_2_kalibo_public_market.speaker: Anong Pedring
scene_2_kalibo_public_market.translation: Where are you headed next, to church?

scene_3_kalibo_cathedral_midday.text: A large church, strong walls, people going in and out — everyday life, not just for festivals.

scene_3_kalibo_cathedral_midday.speaker: Lola Susan
scene_3_kalibo_cathedral_midday.text: Iya \kami \tanan gasimba. Inyo nga \Lola Jonabel \gid, pinakamasueundun.
scene_3_kalibo_cathedral_midday.translation: This is where we all used to go to church. Your Lola Jonabel especially, she was the most devout.

scene_3_kalibo_cathedral_midday.speaker: Lola Jonabel
scene_3_kalibo_cathedral_midday.text: (laughs) Don't believe her, \Apo. We were all equally naughty back then.
The group sits outside the church, Rose holding a town map.

scene_3_kalibo_cathedral_midday.speaker: Rose
scene_3_kalibo_cathedral_midday.text: \Hara, tan-awa. \Mapa it Kalibo. Kon \magtuon ka it mga \lugar, mas \madali ka \makaagto bisan siin.
scene_3_kalibo_cathedral_midday.translation: Here, look at this. Map of Kalibo. If you learn the places, you'll find your way anywhere more easily.

scene_3_kalibo_cathedral_midday.text: What will you say to Rose?

choices.label: This is actually really helpful. Saeamat, Rose.
I'll try to remember the names, no promises though.
A physical map? Can't I just use my phone?

scene_3_kalibo_cathedral_midday.speaker: Rose
scene_3_kalibo_cathedral_midday.text: See, not completely hopeless after all.

scene_3_kalibo_cathedral_midday.speaker: Rose
scene_3_kalibo_cathedral_midday.text: That's more effort than I expected, honestly.

scene_3_kalibo_cathedral_midday.speaker: Rose
scene_3_kalibo_cathedral_midday.text: Sure, and when your phone dies, then what, balikbayan?

scene_3_kalibo_cathedral_midday.speaker: Rose
scene_3_kalibo_cathedral_midday.text: Ro sunod nga \lugar nga aton agtunan hay medyo \maeayo — ro manughaboe it \piña fiber. Iya mo makita ro \matuod nga \ubra it mga \Akeanon.
scene_3_kalibo_cathedral_midday.translation: Next place we'll go is a bit far — the piña weaving area. There you'll see real Aklanon craftsmanship.

scene_4_vocabulary_practice_round_number.text: Before leaving the cathedral grounds, they pass by a small souvenir shop full of colorful items.

scene_4_vocabulary_practice_round_number.speaker: Rose
scene_4_vocabulary_practice_round_number.text: Round two. An-om, pito, waeo, siyam, napueo — six through ten. Finish counting to ten this time.

scene_4_vocabulary_practice_round_number.speaker: Player
scene_4_vocabulary_practice_round_number.text: Isaea, daywa, tatlo, ap-at, lima, an-om, pito, waeo, siyam, napueo. Ten! I did it.

scene_4_vocabulary_practice_round_number.speaker: Rose
scene_4_vocabulary_practice_round_number.text: Not bad. Now, colors — look at the fabrics there.

scene_4_vocabulary_practice_round_number.speaker: Rose
scene_4_vocabulary_practice_round_number.text: Puti — white. Itom — black. Puea — red. Asul — blue. Dueaw — yellow. Berdi — green.

choices.label: I like the puea one — the red one. It really stands out.
Maybe the puti, the white one. Simple.
Honestly, I can't tell half these colors apart yet, sorry Rose.

scene_4_vocabulary_practice_round_number.speaker: Rose
scene_4_vocabulary_practice_round_number.text: Good eye. Bold color for a bold first attempt at counting.

scene_4_vocabulary_practice_round_number.speaker: Rose
scene_4_vocabulary_practice_round_number.text: They'll stick eventually. Nobody gets it all at once.
Rose shows a small stone, then a big stone, for comparison.

scene_4_vocabulary_practice_round_number.speaker: Rose
scene_4_vocabulary_practice_round_number.text: Maisot — small. Mabahoe — big. Mayad — good. Bag-o — new. Daan — old.

scene_4_vocabulary_practice_round_number.speaker: Rose
scene_4_vocabulary_practice_round_number.text: Daya — "this." Haron — "that," closer to me. Dato — "that," farther away. Point when you say it, it's easier.
While walking toward the market, Rose points at food items — fish, chicken, eggs, rice.

scene_4_vocabulary_practice_round_number.speaker: Rose
scene_4_vocabulary_practice_round_number.text: Isda — fish. Manok — chicken. Itlog — egg. Humay — rice. Tinapay — bread. Karne — meat. Baboy — pig.

scene_4_vocabulary_practice_round_number.speaker: Player
scene_4_vocabulary_practice_round_number.text: Okay, that's a lot of food words. Good thing we're heading to the market.

scene_4_vocabulary_practice_round_number.speaker: Rose
scene_4_vocabulary_practice_round_number.text: Exactly why I taught them now. Use it or lose it, balikbayan.
